changes.shows: The rounded upper contour, crossing diagonals and flat lower foot form the typed tensor-like construction; an Omega-like reading remains possible.

The first typed k-like cell has a separate upright and diagonals, followed by a densely overlaid hand loop/fork. Cancellation crosses the group. C alternatives are retained because the hand sign is not separable securely.
The blue hand correction has a left cup, a closed upper-right loop and long oblique descending stem. The looped phi form is favored, but phi and a forked psi reading remain possible.

Two sloping arms meet at a low point, with a short return at the upper right. The raised placement is clear; comparisons with the typed v do not securely settle vee/nu/v or justify replacing the hand attribution. C alternatives retained.

The wavy cancellation passes through avec and stops before the separate hand sign. Its blue stem descends below the looped body and extends to an upper-right arm; it remains live. C alternatives retained.
A short single typewriter horizontal stroke stands before On prend.
The hand L is distinct over the typed capital. Two upper serifed stems and an inward descending middle favor M; W remains possible because the hand stroke obscures the lower contours.
Each label glyph has x-shaped serifed diagonals with a horizontal midline. The first is qualified; the two in the canceled parenthesized label use the same first reading.
A curved comma tail descends beneath the first x cancellation after the live right parenthesis.
The a bowl, v diagonals, e bowl/bar and c curve survive beneath the x strikes.
The parenthesized pair is crossed through; it belongs to the same canceled continuation as avec.
The second cell contains the u cup and right foot together with a y diagonal and curved descending tail. The raw overlap is favored, with single-letter alternatives retained.
The central horizontal is a short single typewriter hyphen.
The final r-shaped cell has an additional tall f-like upper loop and a crossing horizontal bar. No correction order is inferred.
The first k, hand raised star, closing parenthesis, comma, e/t and last k can be distinguished under the x line. The comma is visible below the cancellation and was omitted by C.

changes.shows: The i dot, l/t/d ascenders and each n/e/s/u/a/o/r contour remain legible under the x strikes. C doubt resolved.

After exten, the first cell combines s with dotted i, the second combines dotted i with o, and the third combines o with n; a final n follows. The layered reading is retained first, with the simpler C candidates as alternatives.
A lower g-shaped loop descends beneath the é cell, and a rightward g ear coexists with the e bowl/bar and acute accent. Plain é remains a less favored alternative.
A straight i stem with a separate dot overlaps the o circle. The raised mark is a dot, not a circumflex; C doubt resolved to the raw unlike-letter overlap.
The o has an internal i stem and detached dot; the n has an extra tall l stem and upper-left serif. Both overlapping forms are retained, without inferring the sequence of typing. C doubt resolved.
After the canceled condition de, the following live line begins directly with contrainte.
Rotated upright, the initial acute, crossed t, u, looped d, dotted i and final e/r group are readable. C doubt resolved.
The d/e join and short c/o/m/m group ending with a detached period are visible in the rotated note.
The sign has a long oblique left arm, curled upper-right return and descending stem. The ampersand-like reading is favored over a plain plus, but the compressed construction remains uncertain.
The compressed opening a/s/s-like strokes are followed by o/c and a dotted narrow ending. No secure é/e/s sequence supports associées. C alternatives retained.
The initial a loop, u and crossed x precede a continuous g/r/a/d/u/a/t/i/o/n/s group. Mod2 follows on the next hand line. C doubt resolved.
The g descender, r join, a loop, d ascender, u, acute é and final s are readable after rotation. C and H doubts resolved.
The opening pointed v-like stroke and following short joins favor vrais; compressed middle strokes still permit sans. C alternatives retained.

The first gray loop has its own vertical stem, while a darker upward arrowhead and stem overlap it; a separate forked psi-like sign follows. Raw phi/arrow overlap is favored, but a parenthesis plus arrow and the earlier two-letter candidates remain alternatives.
Two hooked question marks with lower points end the line. No additional closing parenthesis follows them.
